generation: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a realistic production-quality UI design for XDock, a standalone classic desktop bottom dock. Reference image 1 is the USER-SELECTED XLaunch Amber Classic visual target, supplying warm blurred architectural wallpaper and colorful dimensional icon aesthetic. Reference image 2 is the original 2013 DDE desktop screenshot, supplying the BOTTOM DOCK structure. Design ONE focused dock component screen, not a collection of alternatives. Target dimensions 1440 x 480, a natural wide component detail view of the bottom portion of a desktop, no stretching or warped typography. Show warm amber blurred architectural wallpaper filling the upper 390px. No full-screen launcher, no category sidebar, no application grid, no giant branding title, no windows. Along the VERY BOTTOM edge a slender dark warm translucent horizontal full-width dock, about 60px tall, small radius at most 3px, no floating rounded capsule or huge glass slab. Fine bright upper border. Dock apps start at the LEFT edge: an elegant restrained X monogram tile representing XLaunch, Firefox, Files, Terminal, VS Code, VLC, then a thin divider, running unpinned apps GIMP and OBS Studio. Icons about 40px tall with tight 12px gaps, richly colorful and dimensional like the 2013 screenshot and selected launcher. Pinned app indicators small subtle amber dashes under Firefox, Terminal and VS Code; OBS also running. The XLaunch icon is subtly hovered with a compact dark tooltip exactly 'XLaunch' directly above it. No fisheye zoom. Leave the middle of the bottom strip empty like a real functional dock. At far RIGHT a thin divider and compact generic volume/network icons and overflow action. No clock or battery status to avoid invented state. Keep actions legible, aligned and compact. Do not display a Docker whale: XDock is a desktop dock, unrelated to containers. No marketing language, diagrams, annotation arrows or external labels. Architecture constraints (not visible UI): XDock and XLaunch are independent products in separate repos, each targets macOS 26+ and Linux GNOME, KDE Plasma, Xfce and DDE via platform adapters, not dependent on full DDE suite. This image is the standalone XDock amber design aligned to the already selected source, not a new visual direction. Use spacing, thin dividers and surface tint, no individual app cards. Match source warm wallpaper and subtle material precisely.
